three_dimensional_finest_completed.note: 24 mm geometry.  Superseded as the acceptance basis on 2026-09-21: at this length both routes sit below the infinite-length 2-D reference because the end caps are a third of the conductor, and the fractions are measured mid-span.  Retained as provenance

acceptance.margins: beak current fraction 0.28%, beak loss fraction 0.58%, centroid 0.0100 mm against a 0.0894 mm lane spacing, probe-line H 0.17% -- every metric inside its limit by a factor of five or more, and both routes within 0.7% of the independent 2-D reference on all of them
acceptance.scope: a straight constant-section beak fin at 150 kHz in copper, with both discretisations independently converged.  It does not cover tapered or curved fins, brazed separate fin solids, filleted roots, nonlinear or temperature-dependent material, or workpiece back-reaction on the branch currents (gate 4).  Pointwise maximum K remains diagnostic only

length_resolved_2026_09_21.why: h (maxh 0.75 -> 0.45 mm), p (fes_order 0 -> 1) and geometry order (1 -> 2) were each moved on the 24 mm fixture and the delivery fractions followed none of them, while R did.  Both routes lay below the infinite-length 2-D reference in the same order, which points at the fixture length rather than at either discretisation

relative_to_2d_reference.reading: the two routes bracket the reference -- BEM-A just below, PEEC just above, on all three fractions -- which is what two independently converged discretisations do around a true value
